m012:
Rogue Cultivation
Philosophy
"The lone wolf starves, but it
answers to no master. The caged bird
eats well, but never knows the sky."
Rogue Cultivation is not a unified
tradition but rather the absence of one.
Rogue cultivators reject—or are
rejected by—the sect system that
dominates the cultivation world. They
are self-taught wanderers, scavengers
of techniques, survivors who forge
their own path without masters,
resources, or the protection of
institutional power.
Some choose this path willingly,
valuing freedom above all else. Others
are forced into it—sect outcasts,
orphans who never had the chance to
join a proper school, or cultivators
whose sects were destroyed. What
unites all Rogue cultivators is their
independence and their
resourcefulness.
Rogue Cultivation is the hardest path.
Without access to sect libraries, spirit
stones, or inherited techniques, Rogue
cultivators must improvise constantly.

They steal techniques, learn from
chance encounters, and piece together
cultivation methods from fragments
and rumors. Their progression is
slower, more dangerous, and filled with
dead ends.
Yet this struggle breeds resilience.
Rogue cultivators learn to survive on
nothing, to identify opportunities others
miss, and to adapt to any situation.
They are jacks-of-all-trades, masters
of none—but in a world where
specialization can become a fatal
weakness, versatility is its own
strength.
The greatest Rogue cultivators are
legends—individuals who rose from
nothing to shake the heavens, who
proved that determination and cunning
can overcome any disadvantage. The
worst are bandits and desperados,
using stolen techniques for petty
crime. Most fall somewhere in
between: survivors doing what they
must to keep climbing.

Features
Skills: Choose four from: Acrobatics,
Athletics, Deception, Insight,
Intimidation, Investigation, Perception,
Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Survival
Starting Age Requirement: 16+
Primary Stats: Luck (primary),
Perception (secondary), Potential
(tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 8 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d8 (or
5) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor, medium armor
Weapons: Simple weapons, hand
crossbows, longswords,
shortswords, improvised weapons
Tools: Thieves' tools, one artisan
tool of choice
Saving Throws: Luck, Perception
Abilities
Scrappy Survival (LV.1)
You've learned to survive with
nothing. You have advantage on
Survival checks and can always find
enough to eat and drink in any
environment (though it may not be
pleasant). Additionally, you can
identify whether an unknown
technique manual is genuine or fake
with a DC 10 Perception check.
Opportunistic Strike (LV.1)
When you have advantage on an
attack roll, you deal an extra 1d6
damage. This increases to 2d6 at lv.5,
3d6 at lv.10, and 4d6 at lv.15.
Flexible Cultivation (LV.1)
Your lack of formal training has
taught you to adapt. You may learn
techniques from any Path, though you
suffer -1 to cultivation checks when
learning techniques outside your
primary Path. Additionally, you can
combine techniques from different
traditions in creative ways.

Street Wisdom (LV.3)
You gain proficiency in Insight and
Perception if you don't already have it.
If you already have proficiency, you
gain +2 to those checks instead.
Uncanny Dodge (LV.5)
When an attacker you can see hits
you with an attack, you can use your
reaction to halve the attack's damage
against you. (Costs 2 qi)
Unleashed Potential(LV.6)
Your determination and willpower
is your greatest potential. You get +1
to your Potential score and +1 to your
Intelligence.
Treasure Sense (LV.7)
You've developed an instinct for
finding valuable things. You can sense
the presence of valuable cultivation
resources, hidden treasures, or
powerful artifacts within 30 feet. This
sense doesn't tell you exactly what or
where, though.

Desperate Gambit (LV.9)
Once per long rest, when you
would be reduced to 0 HP, you may
make a DC 15 Luck save. On a
success, you instead drop to 1 HP,
immediately move up to your speed
without provoking opportunity attacks,
and your next attack deals double
damage.
Self-Made Immortal (LV.12)
You've proven that formal training
isn't necessary for greatness. Choose
one technique from any Path. You
learn this technique automatically
without needing to make a cultivation
check, and it costs 2*level less qi to
use (minimum 1).
Thousand Faces, Thousand Skills
(LV.15)
Your adaptability reaches its peak.
You can observe someone using a
technique or skill. Make a DC 18
Perception check. On a success, you
can mimic that technique or skill for
24 hours, though at reduced
effectiveness (treat as one tier lower).
You can maintain up to three mimicked
abilities at once.

Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Scavenger's Way
Orthodox Reputation:
Rogue cultivators are viewed with
suspicion by sect members, who see
them as potential thieves or bandits. -2
to initial Persuasion checks with sect
cultivators.

Qi Gathering:
Rogue cultivators gather qi from
any available source—ambient energy,
natural phenomena, or even stealing it
from spirit stones and treasures. Roll
1d20 + Luck modifier. On 15+, gain
1d6 additional qi during meditation.
Breakthrough Difficulty: Medium.
Rogues face standard tribulations,
but without sect support, they must
prepare entirely on their own. +2 to
tribulation damage, but +2 to saves
against tribulation effects (you're used
to hardship).
Technique Compatibility:
Can learn techniques from any
tradition, but suffers -1 penalty to
learning checks for non-Rogue
techniques.

Demonic Temptation:
Without proper guidance, Rogue
cultivators are more susceptible to
demonic techniques and shortcuts. GM
may offer powerful but karmically
dangerous opportunities.
Resource Scarcity:
You typically have 50% fewer
spirit stones and cultivation resources
than sect-backed cultivators of your
level.
m013:
Occult Cultivation
Philosophy
"What the righteous call evil is
merely power they fear to grasp. What
they call taboo is knowledge they lack
the courage to seek."
Occult Cultivation walks the
shadow roads of power—techniques
rejected by orthodox sects, knowledge
preserved in forbidden texts, methods
that extract strength from sources
others consider too dangerous or
immoral to touch. Occult cultivators
are practitioners of the heterodox and
the forbidden, seekers of power
through unconventional and often
disturbing means.
This path encompasses blood
magic, soul manipulation, curse
techniques, and the binding of spirits to
one's will. Occult cultivators deal with
entities most would flee from—ghosts,
demons, eldritch beings from beyond
reality's edge. They make pacts,
perform rituals, and bargain with
forces that operate on principles
foreign to ordinary cultivation.

The line between Occult and
Demonic cultivation is thin. Demonic
cultivation actively harms others and
corrupts the self in pursuit of power.
Occult cultivation merely uses methods
that orthodoxy rejects—some Occult
practitioners are no more evil than any
other cultivator, simply more willing to
explore forbidden knowledge.
Occult techniques often carry
hidden costs—madness, corruption,
karmic debt, or attention from entities
best left undisturbed.
Occult cultivators are pariahsa in
righteous society. Most hide their true
path, pretending to practice acceptable
methods while secretly pursuing
forbidden knowledge. Others embrace
their status, joining demonic sects or
establishing their own dark sanctuaries
where they can practice freely.
The greatest Occult cultivators
become legends of terror—beings of
immense power feared throughout the
realms.

Features
Skills:
Choose three from: Arcana, Deception,
History, Insight, Intimidation,
Investigation, Perception, Religion
Starting Age Requirement:
18+
Primary Stats:
Perception (primary), Charisma
(secondary), Potential (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 6 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d6 (or
4) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor
Weapons: Simple weapons, ritual
daggers, staves, whips
Tools: Calligrapher's supplies, one
set of artisan tools related to ritual
work
Saving Throws:
Perception, Charisma
Abilities
Forbidden Knowledge (LV.1)
You have studied texts most would
burn. You gain proficiency in Arcana
and Religion. You can identify curses,
hexes, and occult phenomena with a
DC 12 Perception check. Additionally,
you can read and understand
forbidden texts without suffering
mental damage (though the knowledge
itself may still be dangerous).
Blood Offering (LV.1)
You can sacrifice your own vitality
to power your techniques. As a bonus
action, you may take up to 10 HP
damage (cannot reduce you below 1
HP) to gain ten times that much qi.
This qi must be used within 1 minute,
or it dissipates. Using this ability
generates +1 Karma per use.
Spirit Sight (LV.1)
You can see spirits, ghosts, and
ethereal beings automatically without
needing to make checks. You can also
see through illusions with a DC 12
Perception check.

Occult Ritual (LV.3)
You can perform extended rituals
to achieve powerful effects. Rituals
take 1-8 hours and require specific
components. Examples include:
summoning spirits for information,
creating temporary protective barriers,
cursing distant enemies, or communing
with dead souls. Each ritual costs 10 qi
and generates +2 Karma.
Dark Pact (LV.5)
You may form a pact with an
otherworldly entity (spirit, demon, or
stranger thing). Work with your GM to
define the entity and the pact's terms.
You gain a unique ability from your
patron, but you also gain an obligation.
Breaking the pact has severe
consequences.
Example pacts:
Shadow Patron: Gain advantage
on Stealth checks and deal +1d6
necrotic damage with attacks.
Obligation: Must spend 1 hour per
day in complete darkness.
Blood Ancestor: Gain +10 max HP
and resistance to necrotic
damage. Obligation: Must make a
blood offering (2 HP) each dawn.

Void Entity: Gain +2 to Perception
and can see invisible creatures.
Obligation: Must never refuse
knowledge offered to you.
Curse Weaving (LV.7)
You can place curses on enemies.
As an action, spend 8 qi and choose a
target within 60 feet who can see or
hear you. The target makes a DC 15
Charisma save. On a failure, choose
one effect:
Curse of Weakness: -2 to all
attack rolls for 24 hours
Curse of Misfortune: Disadvantage
on saving throws for 1 hour
Curse of Pain: Target takes 2d6
necrotic damage at the start of
each of their turns for 1 minute.
Placing a curse generates +3
Karma.
Soul Harvest (LV.9)
When you reduce a creature to 0
HP, you may attempt to harvest part
of its soul. Make a DC 14 Perception
check. On a success, gain 2d8
temporary HP and 1d6 temporary qi
(lasts until your next long rest). Using
this ability generates +2 Karma.

Forbidden Ascension (LV.12)
Your understanding of occult
principles allows you to bypass normal
cultivation limitations. Once per long
rest, you may use any technique
regardless of whether you meet its
requirements. However, roll a d20. On
a 1-5, you suffer a backlash: take
3d10 necrotic damage and gain +5
Karma.
Architect of Nightmares (LV.15)
You can reshape reality in limited
ways. Once per long rest, you may
spend 10 minutes performing a ritual to
create one of the following effects
within a 60-foot radius:
Summon a fog that causes
hallucinations (all creatures
except you have disadvantage on
attack rolls)
Animate shadows to physically
attack enemies (3 shadow
servants, each with 20 HP and +6
to hit, dealing 2d6 necrotic
damage)
Create a zone where the dead can
speak and spirits manifest
physically These effects last for 1
hour. Generates +5 Karma.

Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Forbidden Path
Pariah Status:
Righteous cultivators react with
hostility if they discover your Path. -4
to Persuasion checks with orthodox
cultivators. May be attacked on sight
in some regions.
Karma Accumulation:
Occult techniques often generate
Karma. You must carefully manage
your Karma balance or face severe
tribulations.
Power Cost:
Many Occult abilities have hidden
prices. The GM may introduce
unexpected consequences for frequent
use of forbidden techniques.

Qi Gathering:
Occult cultivators draw qi from
taboo sources—graveyards, sites of
tragedy, cursed locations, or through
pacts with entities. Gain +2 to
cultivation checks when cultivating in
"dark" locations, but -2 in temples or
righteous sects.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Hard. Heaven views Occult
cultivation with suspicion. Tribulations
deal +3 damage, and you must make
an additional Charisma save (DC 15)
to resist spiritual corruption during a
breakthrough. Failure adds +3 Karma.
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns occult, curse, blood,
soul, and summoning techniques.
Cannot learn Buddhist or other "pure"
techniques.

Temptation:
You have access to powerful
shortcuts. Resist the urge to sacrifice
long-term growth for immediate power.
m014:
Body Refinement Cultivation
Philosophy
"The body is the foundation upon
which all cultivation rests. Strengthen
the foundation, and you may build a
tower that touches heaven.”
While most cultivators view the
physical body as merely a vessel for
qi, Body Refinement cultivators see it
as the cultivation itself. They forge
their flesh into spiritual metal,
transform their bones into unbreakable
jade, and refine their blood into liquid
qi. For them, the body is not a
limitation to transcend but a
masterpiece to perfect.
Body Refinement is among the
oldest cultivation methods, predating
even the formal sect system. Ancient
warriors discovered that by tempering
their bodies with qi, exposure to
extreme conditions, and consuming
powerful materials, they could achieve
strength that rivaled—or exceeded—
those who focused purely on spiritual
cultivation.

This path requires incredible
dedication and pain tolerance. Body
Refinement cultivators subject
themselves to brutal training: bathing in
cauldrons of medicinal liquid, striking
their bodies against iron and stone,
circulating qi through muscles and
organs until they burn with power.
Each advancement brings physical
agony as the body literally tears itself
apart and rebuilds stronger.
Yet the rewards are substantial.
Body Refinement cultivators are nearly
impossible to kill—their bodies shrug
off wounds that would be fatal to
others, they can fight for days without
tiring, and their physical strength can
shatter mountains. They are the
frontline warriors, the unstoppable
juggernauts who wade into battle
confident that few can harm them.
The greatest challenge of Body
Refinement is balance. Focusing too
heavily on the physical without
spiritual cultivation leads to a powerful
but limited path—a body that can
survive anything but a mind and soul
that remain mortal.

Features
Skills:
Choose three from: Acrobatics,
Athletics, Endurance, Intimidation,
Medicine, Perception, Survival
Starting Age Requirement:
14+
Primary Stats:
Potential (primary), Constitution
(secondary), Luck (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 12 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d12 (or
7) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor, medium
armor, heavy armor (though many
prefer fighting unarmored)
Weapons: Simple weapons, martial
weapons
Tools: None required
Saving Throws:
Potential, Constitution
Abilities
Iron Body (LV.1)
Your body has been tempered
beyond normal limits. When not
wearing armor, your AC equals 10 +
Constitution modifier + Potential
modifier. You can still use a shield and
gain this benefit.

Pain Tolerance (LV.3)
You've trained your body to
endure incredible punishment. You
have an advantage on saves against
effects that would cause pain,
exhaustion, or incapacitation.
Additionally, you can function
normally even when at low HP (no
penalties until you reach 0 HP).

Unarmed Combat Master (LV.1)
Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 +
Potential modifier damage. This
increases to 1d8 at 5th realm, 1d10 at
10th realm, and 1d12 at 15th realm.
Your unarmed strikes count as magical
for the purpose of overcoming
resistance.

Body Regeneration (LV.5)
Your refined body heals at an
accelerated rate. You regain additional
HP equal to your Constitution modifier
(minimum 1) at the start of each of
your turns while you're conscious and
above 0 HP. This healing increases to
double your Constitution modifier at
level 10.

Qi-Tempered Flesh (LV.1)
You can spend qi to temporarily
enhance your body. As a bonus action,
spend 3 qi to gain one of the following
for 1 minute:
+2 to AC
+2 to attack and damage rolls
Advantage on Potential or
Constitution saves
Resistance to one damage type of
your choice
Immovable Stance (LV.5)
You cannot be moved against your
will while standing on solid ground.
You can have an advantage on saves
and checks to resist being pushed,
pulled, knocked prone, or teleported.
Additionally, you can spend 4 qi as a
reaction to automatically succeed on
such a save or check.

Diamond Bones (LV.7)
Your bones have been refined to
near-indestructibility. You gain
resistance to bludgeoning, piercing,
and slashing damage from non-magical
sources. Magical sources still deal full
damage unless otherwise resisted.
Titanic Strength (LV.9)
Your Potential score increases by
+2 (this can exceed normal
maximum). Additionally, you count as
one size larger for determining
carrying capacity and the creatures
you can grapple or push.

Transcendent Physique (LV.15)
Your body has transcended mortal
limitations entirely. You gain the
following benefits:
Immunity to poison and disease
No longer need to eat, drink, or
breathe (though you can if
desired)
Age at 1/10th normal rate
Automatically stabilize when at 0
HP
Can survive in any environment
(extreme heat, cold, vacuum,
underwater)
Your unarmed strikes deal an
additional 2d12 damage
Unbreakable Will (LV.12)
Your perfected body houses an
unshakeable spirit. You become
immune to fear, charm, and mind
control effects. Additionally, once per
long rest, when you would fail a saving
throw, you can choose to succeed
instead.

Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Flesh Forging
Obvious Power:
Your refined body is visibly
different—more muscular, tougher skin,
unusual resilience. People recognize
you as a Body Refinement cultivator
easily.

Qi Gathering:
Body Refinement cultivators
absorb qi directly into their bodies
rather than storing it in a dantian. They
can cultivate by enduring physical
hardship, bathing in medicinal
solutions, or consuming spirit beast
meat. Gain +2 to cultivation checks
when cultivating through physical
training.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Medium. Breakthroughs require
intense physical tribulation—your body
must be broken down and rebuilt.
Tribulations deal +2 damage but you
have +2 to Constitution saves during
tribulation.
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns body enhancement,
physical combat, and endurance
techniques. Struggles with ranged or
purely spiritual techniques (-2 to
learning checks for non-physical
techniques).

Physical Focus:
You excel in direct combat but
may struggle with subtle or spiritual
challenges.
Resource Intensive:
Body Refinement requires
medicinal baths, spirit beast meat, and
other physical resources. Budget
accordingly.
Pain Tolerance:
You're expected to endure
hardship without complaint. Showing
weakness is considered shameful
among Body Refinement practitioners.
m015:
Poison Cultivation
Philosophy
"A single drop can kill an emperor.
A single breath can topple a sect. Let
others seek power through brute force
—I will find it in subtlety.”
Poison Cultivation is the art of
toxins, venoms, and corrosive
substances refined to supernatural
potency. Poison cultivators are
alchemists of death, transforming
mundane substances into lethal
weapons, turning their own bodies into
vessels of concentrated venom, and
wielding toxicity as both tool and
cultivation method.
This path has ancient roots in
assassin clans, physician families who
understood that medicine and poison
are two sides of the same coin, and
hermits who lived in toxic
environments and learned to thrive.
Poison cultivators see toxicity not as
destruction but as transformation—a
poison kills by fundamentally changing
what it touches, and is that not
cultivation's essence?

Poison Cultivation walks a
dangerous line. It is heterodox but not
necessarily evil—many poison
cultivators are physicians who
understand that dose makes the
poison, or defenders who use toxins to
level the playing field against
physically superior opponents. Yet the
path attracts its share of assassins and
murderers, giving all poison cultivators
a sinister reputation.
The practice is deeply technical.
Poison cultivators must understand
countless substances, their
interactions, and how spiritual energy
modifies their effects. They experiment
constantly, often on themselves,
gradually building immunity to their
own toxins while making their bodies
produce ever-more-deadly
compounds.
The greatest danger is corruption—
not moral but physical. Poison
cultivators who fail to properly
balance their toxins can poison
themselves, suffering from chronic
conditions, shortened lifespans, or
horrific mutations.

Features
Skills:
Choose three from:
Arcana, Investigation, Medicine,
Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand,
Stealth, Survival
Starting Age Requirement:
16+
Primary Stats:
Perception (primary), Potential
(secondary), Constitution (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 8 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d8 (or
5) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor
Weapons: Simple weapons,
blowguns, darts, needles,
shortswords, whips
Tools: Alchemist's supplies,
poisoner's kit
Saving Throws:
Perception, Constitution
Abilities
Poison Immunity (LV.1)
Through careful exposure, you've
built immunity to most toxins. You
have advantage on saves against
poison and resistance to poison
damage. At level 7, this becomes full
immunity to poison.
Toxic Touch (LV.1)
You can coat your weapons or
unarmed strikes with poison as a
bonus action (costs 2 qi). The next
attack that hits deals an additional 1d6
poison damage, and the target must
make a DC 12 Constitution save or
become poisoned for 1 minute. This
damage increases to 2d6 at level 5,
3d6 at level 10, and 4d6 at level 15.
Poison Crafting (LV.1)
You can craft poisons during
downtime. Given access to materials
and 1 hour of work, you can create
doses of poison. Roll Perception +
Potential:
10-14: Basic poison (1d6 damage,
DC 12 save)
15-19: Potent poison (2d6
damage, DC 14 save, effect)
20+: Lethal poison (3d6 damage,
DC 16 save, major effect)
Venomous Body (LV.3)
Your body begins producing
natural toxins. Creatures that bite or
swallow you take 2d6 poison damage.
Additionally, you can spend 4 qi to
exhale a 10-foot cone of poisonous
gas (DC 13 Constitution save or take
2d6 poison damage and become
poisoned for 1 round).
Toxin Resistance (LV.3)
You gain resistance to acid and
necrotic damage. Your experience with
destructive substances has hardened
you against corrosive forces.

Delayed Venom (LV.5)
When you apply poison to a target,
you can make it delayed. Instead of
taking effect immediately, the poison
activates after a time of your choosing
(1 minute to 24 hours). The target
makes their save when the poison
activates. This is excellent for
assassination or creating timed traps.
Corrosive Qi (LV.7)
Your qi becomes inherently toxic.
All your qi-based attacks deal an
additional 1d8 poison damage.
Additionally, you can spend 6 qi as an
action to corrode non-magical objects
(weapons, armor, walls) within 15 feet
—they lose 10 AC and take 4d6 acid
damage.
Poison Immunity Stripping (LV.9)
You've developed toxins so potent
they bypass normal immunities. When
you deal poison damage to a creature
with resistance or immunity to poison,
treat resistance as normal damage and
immunity as resistance. Additionally,
your poisons affect undead and
constructs (though at half damage).

Miasma Aura (LV.12)
Your body constantly emits a
subtle toxic aura. As an action, you
can amplify this aura for 1 minute
(costs 10 qi). While active, all
creatures within 15 feet of you must
make a DC 16 Constitution save at the
start of their turn or take 3d6 poison
damage and have disadvantage on
attack rolls. Allies can be excluded.
Thousand Poison Immortal Body (15)
You have transformed your body
into a living vessel of ultimate toxicity.
You gain the following benefits:
Your blood, sweat, and breath are
all poisonous (creatures in contact
take 2d8 poison damage)
You can spend 15 qi to create a
30-foot radius death cloud that
lasts 1 minute (DC 18 Constitution
save or take 6d6 poison damage
and become paralyzed for 1
round)
Once per long rest, you can inject
yourself with any poison to
immediately convert it to qi (gain
qi equal to the poison's damage
dice total)
Your poison damage ignores all
resistance and immunity
Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Toxic Refinement
Feared Reputation:
Poison cultivators are feared and
often unwelcome. -3 to Persuasion
checks in orthodox settings. Some
cities ban known poison cultivators.

Qi Gathering:
Poison cultivators cultivate by
exposing themselves to increasingly
potent toxins and surviving. They can
gain cultivation progress by consuming
poisons, meditating in toxic
environments, or refining venomous
spirit beasts. Gain +2 to cultivation
checks when cultivating in poisonous
locations.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Medium-Hard. Your tribulations
often involve purging accumulated
toxins from your body. Take +1
damage from tribulations, but gain
advantage on Constitution saves during
breakthrough. Failure can result in
permanent toxin buildup (cumulative
-1 to Constitution until healed).
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns poison, acid, disease,
and debuff techniques. Struggles with
pure/holy techniques (-3 to learning
checks for radiant or cleansing
techniques).

Physician's Knowledge:
Your understanding of toxins
makes you an excellent healer. You
have advantage on Medicine checks
related to treating poison or disease.
Expensive Path:
Crafting and experimenting with
poisons requires constant resources.
Budget for materials.
Moral Ambiguity:
Using poison is often seen as
dishonorable or cowardly. Be prepared
to justify your methods.
m016:
Sword Cultivation
Philosophy
"The sword is not a tool. It is an
extension of the self, a manifestation of
will made steel. Master the sword, and
you master yourself.”
Sword Cultivation is perhaps the
most iconic and revered of all
cultivation paths. It is the way of the
blade—not merely learning to fight with
a sword, but becoming one with it,
transforming the weapon into an
extension of the cultivator's dao. For
Sword cultivators, the blade is
everything: weapon, companion,
teacher, and ultimate expression of
their path.
This tradition stretches back to the
first immortals who discovered that a
sword, when imbued with qi and will,
could cut through anything—armor,
formations, even the fabric of reality
itself. Over millennia, countless sword
immortals have contributed to this
path, creating sword techniques that
range from simple cutting methods to
reality-warping sword daos.

Sword Cultivation emphasizes
purity, focus, and decisive action. A
Sword cultivator's strength lies in their
ability to concentrate all their power
into a single point—the edge of their
blade. Where others disperse their qi
across many techniques, the Sword
cultivator channels everything through
their weapon, achieving devastating
cutting power.
The path requires absolute
dedication. Sword cultivators bond
with their blades through blood, qi, and
shared experience. The greatest
practitioners forge their own swords
using rare materials and their own
essence, creating weapons that grow
stronger alongside them. Some even
achieve Sword Spirit awakening,
where their blade gains consciousness
and becomes a true partner.
Sword Cultivation has many subschools: the elegant and precise Path
of Flowing Water, the aggressive Path
of Severing Mountains, the mysterious
Path of Void Cutting, and countless
others. Yet all share the fundamental
belief that through the sword, one can
cut through any obstacle.

Features
Skills:
Choose three from:
Acrobatics, Athletics, History, Insight,
Intimidation, Perception
Starting Age Requirement:
12+
Primary Stats:
Potential (primary), Perception
(secondary), Luck (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 10 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d10 (or
6) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor, medium armor
Weapons: All swords (shortsword,
longsword, greatsword, dao, jian,
etc.), and daggers
Tools: Smith's tools
Saving Throws:
Potential, Perception
Abilities
Sword Bond (LV.1)
Choose one sword to become your
bonded weapon. While wielding it, you
gain +1 to attack and damage rolls. If
you lose this sword, you can perform
a 1-hour ritual to bond with a new one.
Your bonded sword cannot be used
effectively by others (-2 to their
attack rolls).
Sword Qi (LV.1)
You can extend your qi through
your blade, increasing its cutting
power. As a bonus action, spend 2 qi
to add 1d8 force damage to your next
sword attack. This increases to 2d8 at
level 5, 3d8 at level 10, and 4d8 at
level 15.
Flowing Blade Style (LV.1)
When you take the Dodge action,
you can still make one sword attack
as a bonus action.

Sword Meditation (LV.3)
You can meditate while performing
sword forms. When you cultivate while
practicing with your sword, you gain
+2 to your cultivation check.
Additionally, you can enter a
meditative state while fighting, gaining
advantage on your next attack after
spending 1 full round observing an
opponent.
Blade Deflection (LV.3)
When a creature you can see
attacks you with a weapon, you can
use your reaction to add +3 to your
AC against that attack. If the attack
misses, you can immediately make one
sword attack against the attacker
(costs 3 qi).
Sword Intent (LV.5)
Your will manifests through your
blade. You can make ranged sword
attacks by projecting qi slashes.
Range: 30 feet. These attacks deal
your normal sword damage + 1d10
force damage—costs 4 qi per attack.

Flash Step (LV.5)
As a bonus action, spend 5 qi to
teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied
space you can see. If you teleport to a
space within 5 feet of a creature, you
have advantage on your next sword
attack against them.
Sword Heart (LV.7)
Your dedication to the sword has
purified your spirit. You gain
advantage on saves against fear,
charm, and illusion effects.
Additionally, you can sense hostile
intent directed at you (cannot be
surprised while conscious and wielding
your bonded sword).
Thousand Cuts (LV.9)
Once per short rest, you can attack
with impossible speed. When you take
the Attack action, you can make up to
four sword attacks instead of your
normal number of attacks. Each attack
after the first costs 3 qi.
Sword Domain (LV.12)
Your mastery creates a field where
your sword reigns supreme. As an
action, spend 10 qi to activate Sword
Domain for 1 minute. Within 30 feet of
you:
You have advantage on all sword
attack rolls
Enemies have disadvantage on
saves against your sword
techniques
You can make opportunity attacks
with your sword without using
your reaction
Your Sword Intent range increases
to 60 feet
One Sword Cuts Heaven (LV.15)
You have achieved the peak of
sword cultivation. Once per long rest,
you can unleash a legendary sword
strike. Spend 20 qi and make one
attack roll with advantage. On a hit:
Deal your weapon damage +
10d10 force damage
The target must make a DC 20
Constitution save or be bisected
(instant death if under 100 HP)
The sword energy continues in a
100-foot line, dealing 8d10 force
damage to all creatures in the line
(DC 18 Dexterity save for half)
This attack can cut through any
non-magical material and most
magical barriers
Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Sword Unity
Honorable Reputation:
Sword cultivators are generally
respected as honorable warriors. +2 to
Persuasion checks with orthodox
cultivators.

Qi Gathering:
Sword cultivators gather qi by
communing with their blade, practicing
sword forms, and understanding the
nature of sharpness and severance.
Gain +2 to cultivation checks when
meditating with your bonded sword.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Medium. Your tribulations test your
sword heart—you must face illusions
that challenge your dedication to the
path. Standard tribulation damage, but
you have advantage on saves if
wielding your bonded sword.
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns all sword techniques
and cutting/slicing techniques.
Struggles with healing, defensive, or
non-blade techniques (-2 to learning
checks for non-sword techniques).

Weapon Dependency:
Your power is tied to your sword.
Losing your bonded weapon severely
weakens you until you can bond with
a new one.
Sword Culture:
You're expected to know sword
etiquette, famous sword immortals, and
the histories of legendary blades.
Single-Minded Focus: You excel at
direct combat but may struggle with
subtle or non-combat challenges.
m017:
Buddhist Cultivation
Philosophy
"All suffering stems from
attachment. All power stems from
desire. To cultivate is to walk the
razor's edge between transcendence
and temptation.”
Buddhist Cultivation is the path of
enlightenment through spiritual
refinement, combining the teachings of
ancient Buddhist philosophy with the
techniques of qi manipulation. Buddhist
cultivators seek to transcend the cycle
of karma and rebirth not through force
or accumulation of power, but through
understanding the fundamental nature
of existence and releasing attachment
to the illusory self.
This path originated in sacred
monasteries where monks discovered
that meditation, when combined with qi
circulation, could achieve states of
consciousness far beyond ordinary
enlightenment. They developed
techniques that emphasized internal
peace, karmic purification, and the
transformation of suffering into
strength.

Buddhist cultivators are not
necessarily pacifists, though many lean
that direction. They understand that
existence involves struggle and that
sometimes force is necessary to
protect others or oneself. However,
they strive to act without hatred, to
fight without malice, and to overcome
enemies by first overcoming
themselves.
The path emphasizes three core
principles: Discipline (controlling
desires and impulses), Compassion
(understanding that all beings suffer),
and Wisdom (seeing through illusions
to reality's true nature). Buddhist
cultivators develop powerful defensive
techniques, karmic purification
methods, and abilities that target the
spirit rather than the body.
Perhaps uniquely among cultivation
paths, Buddhist Cultivation actively
seeks to reduce karma rather than
accumulate it. Buddhist cultivators gain
power not by taking but by giving, not
by dominating but by understanding.
This makes their progression slower
but more stable.

Features
Acrobatics, Athletics, History, Insight,
Medicine, Perception, Persuasion,
Religion
Starting Age Requirement:
10+
Primary Stats:
Perception (primary), Charisma
(secondary), Constitution (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 10 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d10 (or
6) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: None (rely on Dharma
Protection), or simple robes
Weapons: Simple weapons,
staves, monk weapons (fists, rope
darts, etc.)
Tools: Calligrapher's supplies
Saving Throws:
Perception, Charisma
Skills:
Choose three from:
Abilities
Dharma Protection (LV.1)
When not wearing armor or using a
shield, your AC equals 10 +
Perception modifier + Charisma
modifier + any bonus from cultivation
realm. This represents spiritual
protection through inner peace.
Karmic Clarity (LV.1)
You can sense karmic weight. By
spending 1 minute observing a
creature, location, or object, make a
DC 12 Perception check to sense its
karmic burden (whether it's associated
with good or evil deeds). Additionally,
all your techniques generate 50% less
karma (round down).
Merciful Strike (LV.1)
When you reduce a creature to 0
HP, you can choose to knock them
unconscious instead of killing them,
regardless of damage dealt. This
generates no karma. You can also
spend 3 qi to make any attack nonlethal, dealing full damage but only
knocking unconscious.

Inner Peace (LV.3)
You have advantage on saves
against fear, charm, and effects that
would cause rage or loss of control.
Additionally, you can enter a
meditative trance as a bonus action
(costs 2 qi), gaining resistance to
psychic damage and advantage on
Perception checks for 1 minute.
Healing Palm (LV.3)
As an action, you can touch a
creature and spend qi to heal them.
For every 20 qi spent, heal 1d8 HP
(maximum 60 qi per use at this level,
increasing to 100 qi at 7th and 150 qi
at 12th). This generates -1 karma per
use.
Lotus Position Defense (LV.5)
When you spend your action
meditating in one place, you gain the
following until your next turn:
+5 AC
Resistance to all damage
Advantage on all saving throws
Automatic success on
concentration checks You can still
use bonus actions and reactions
while in this state.

Six Senses (LV.5)
Your spiritual awareness expands
dramatically. You gain blindsight out to
30 feet and can detect invisible or
ethereal creatures within this range.
Additionally, you can sense strong
emotions in creatures within 60 feet.
Karmic Reversal (LV.7)
Once per short rest, when a
creature within 30 feet attacks you or
an ally, you can use your reaction to
force them to confront their karmic
burden. They must make a DC 15
Charisma save. On a failure, they take
psychic damage equal to their negative
karma × 2 and must use their action to
reflect on their deeds (effectively
stunned for 1 round). On a success,
they take half damage.
Diamond Body (LV.9)
Your body becomes nearly
indestructible through spiritual
refinement. You gain resistance to all
physical damage (slashing, piercing,
bludgeoning). Additionally, you cannot
be aged magically, are immune to
disease, and no longer need food or
water (though you can still consume
them).

Ten Thousand Buddha Palm (12)
As an action, spend 12 qi to create
a massive golden palm of Buddhist
energy that strikes all hostile creatures
in a 30-foot radius around you. Each
creature must make a DC 17 Charisma
save:
Failure: Takes 6d10 radiant
damage and is knocked prone
Success: Takes half damage and
is not knocked prone
Evil creatures (karma > 10): Take
an additional 4d10 radiant damage
and are stunned for 1 round. This
technique generates -2 karma.
Bodhisattva Aspect (LV.15)
Once per long rest, you can
channel the aspect of an enlightened
being for 10 minutes. While in this
state:
You gain 50 temporary HP
Your Dharma Protection grants +5
AC
All healing you perform is doubled
You gain flying speed equal to
your walking speed
You emit an aura of peace (all
allies within 30 feet have
advantage on saves)
Evil creatures that start their turn
within 30 feet of you take 3d10
radiant damage
Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Enlightenment Path
Respected Status:
Buddhist cultivators are generally
trusted and respected. +3 to
Persuasion checks with most NPCs.
Even demonic cultivators often show
grudging respect.

Qi Gathering:
Buddhist cultivators gather qi
through meditation, acts of
compassion, and karmic purification.
They can cultivate anywhere but gain
+3 to cultivation checks in temples,
during acts of mercy, or after helping
others without seeking reward.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Easy-Medium. Buddhist cultivators
face lighter tribulations due to their
karmic purity. Tribulations deal -2
damage, and you gain +2 to all saves
during breakthrough. If your karma is
positive (negative number), reduce
tribulation difficulty further.
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns defensive, healing,
psychic, and radiant techniques.
Cannot learn demonic or blood
techniques. Struggles with aggressive
offensive techniques(-2 on cultivation
checks for these).

Karmic Balance:
You must maintain good karma (a
negative number in this system).
Committing evil acts conflicts with
your path and may cause you to lose
abilities until you atone.
Vows:
Many Buddhist cultivators take
vows (no killing, no lying,
vegetarianism, etc.). These are
optional, but generate -1 karma per
day maintained.
Non-Attachment:
You should avoid becoming too
attached to possessions, relationships,
or desires. This can be challenging in a
cultivation world focused on gaining
power.
m018:
Shaman (Wu) Cultivation
Philosophy
"The spirits were here before us
and will remain after. We do not
command them—we walk alongside
them, speaking the language of earth
and sky.”
Shaman Cultivation, known as Wu
Dao, is one of the most ancient
cultivation paths, predating the formal
sect system by millennia. Shamans are
intermediaries between the mortal
world and the spirit realm, cultivators
who gain power not through internal
refinement alone but through
communion with the spiritual forces
that permeate reality.
Unlike most cultivators who see
spirits as resources to bind or
subjugate, Shamans form partnerships
with them. They learn the old
languages—the speech of wind, the
song of stone, the whispers of water.
Through these relationships, Shamans
can call upon spirits for aid, channel
their power, and navigate the liminal
spaces between worlds.

Wu Dao originated in tribal
societies where shamans served as
healers, spiritual guides, and
protectors. These early practitioners
discovered that certain individuals
could perceive and interact with spirits
naturally, and through cultivation, this
gift could be refined into extraordinary
power.
The path emphasizes balance,
respect, and reciprocity. Shamans give
offerings to spirits, perform rituals to
maintain cosmic balance, and serve as
mediators in conflicts between the
material and spiritual worlds. Their
power comes when a Shaman acts in
accordance with natural law and
maintains good relationships with
spirits; they can accomplish feats that
seem miraculous.
Shamans excel at divination, spirit
communication, healing, curse
breaking, and environmental
manipulation. They can sense
disturbances in natural order, predict
weather patterns by reading spiritual
currents, and even temporarily
incarnate powerful spirits to access
their abilities.

Features
Animal Handling, Arcana, Insight,
Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion,
Survival
Starting Age Requirement:
12+
Primary Stats:
Charisma (primary), Perception
(secondary), Luck (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 8 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d8 (or
5) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor
Weapons: Simple weapons,
staves, ritual daggers, bone
weapons
Tools: Herbalism kit, divination
tools (bones, shells, etc.)
Saving Throws:
Charisma, Perception
Skills:
Choose four from:
Abilities
Spirit Sight (LV.1)
You can perceive spirits, ghosts,
and ethereal beings automatically.
Additionally, you can see the "spiritual
resonance" of locations, identifying
places of power, cursed sites, or spirit
gathering points with a DC 10
Perception check.
Spirit Pact (LV.1)
You have formed relationships with
1d4+1 minor spirits (work with your
GM to define them—nature spirits,
ancestor spirits, animal spirits, etc.).
As an action, you can call upon one
spirit to assist you (costs 3 qi):
Guardian Spirit: Grants +2 AC for
1 minute
Healing Spirit: Restores
1d8+Charisma modifier HP to you
or an ally
Messenger Spirit: Delivers a
message to any location within 10
miles
Scout Spirit: Scouts an area up to
1 mile away and reports back
You maintain relationships with spirits
as you advance (gain 1 additional
spirit contact per 2 levels).

Ritual Casting (LV.1)
You can perform extended rituals
to achieve powerful effects. Rituals
take 10 minutes to 1 hour and require
offerings (incense, food, spirit stones,
etc.). Make a Charisma + Perception
check:
DC 12: Minor effect (locate water,
predict tomorrow's weather,
communicate with nearby animal)
DC 15: Moderate effect (remove
curse, heal disease, create
protective ward)
DC 18: Major effect (speak with
the dead, divine distant events,
temporarily enhance ally abilities)
DC 20+: Powerful effect (GM
discretion)
Natural Affinity (LV.3)
You have advantage on checks to
interact with animals, plants, and
natural phenomena. Beasts with
intelligence 3 or lower will not attack
you unless provoked or magically
compelled.

Ancestral Guidance (LV.3)
Once per long rest, you can
commune with ancestor spirits for
guidance. Ask one yes/no question
about a course of action. The GM
answers truthfully based on what your
ancestors would know. Additionally,
once per short rest, you can add 1d6
to any check by briefly channeling
ancestral wisdom.
Spirit Channel (LV.5)
You can temporarily house a spirit
within your body, gaining its abilities.
As an action, spend 6 qi to invite a
willing spirit into your body for up to
10 minutes. While channeling:
Gain the spirit's damage resistance
or immunity
Gain one ability from the spirit
(flight, elemental damage, special
sense, etc.)
Your physical form may partially
manifest the spirit's appearance
After channeling ends, you gain 1
level of exhaustion.

Totem Form (LV.7)
You can assume the form of your
totem animal (chosen at this realm). As
an action, spend 8 qi to transform for
up to 1 hour. In totem form:
Gain that animal's movement
modes (flight, swimming, climbing,
etc.)
Gain advantage on Perception
checks using that animal's primary
sense
Can communicate with animals of
that type
Retain your mental stats but gain
the totem's physical stats if higher
Can cast Shaman techniques but
not use weapons or complex tools
Mass Spirit Calling (LV.9)
You can call upon multiple spirits
simultaneously. As an action, spend 12
qi to summon 2d4 spirit servants that
last for 1 hour. Each spirit has 30 HP,
+8 to hit, deals 2d6 force damage, and
can perform simple tasks. They
understand your commands
telepathically.

World Walker (LV.12)
You can step between the material
and spirit worlds. As an action, spend
10 qi to shift into the spirit realm for
up to 1 hour. While there:
Spirit King/Queen (LV.15)
You have achieved the highest
relationship with the spirit world. You
gain the following permanent benefits:
You become incorporeal in the
material world (can't affect or be
affected by it)
You can travel at 3× your normal
speed
You can communicate freely with
all spirits
You can observe events in the
material world You can return to
the material world as a bonus
action at any location you've
visited before within 100 miles.

All spirits treat you with respect
and deference
You can call upon 1 major spirit
per long rest (equivalent to a CR
10 creature, GM discretion)
Your Spirit Channel ability no
longer causes exhaustion
You can perform rituals in 1/4 the
normal time
Once per long rest, you can ask
the spirit world for a miracle
(major effect, GM discretion, but
spirits will grant it if possible)
You gain the ability to see and
interact with fate threads (limited
precognition)
Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Harmonic
Resonance
Spiritual Obligations:
You must maintain good
relationships with spirits through
regular offerings and respect.
Neglecting spirits causes you to lose
access to their aid.

Qi Gathering:
Shamans cultivate by harmonizing
with natural and spiritual energies.
They gain qi through rituals, offerings
to spirits, and meditation in places of
power. Gain +3 to cultivation checks
when cultivating in natural
environments or sacred sites.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Medium. Your tribulations test your
relationships with spirits and your
understanding of balance. Standard
tribulation damage, but spirits may
intervene to assist you (GM discretion
—once per breakthrough, reduce
damage by 3d10).
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns spirit, nature,
divination, and healing techniques.
Struggles with purely technological or
artificially-created techniques (-2 to
learning checks for formation,
alchemy, or mechanical techniques).

Cultural Respect:
Traditional Shamans follow specific
taboos and protocols. Breaking these
can anger spirits.
Varied Reputation:
Orthodox cultivators may view you
as primitive or superstitious. Locals
and rural folk often respect and seek
out Shamans.
Environmental Connection:
Your power waxes and wanes with
the health of the local environment. In
spiritually dead or corrupted areas,
you suffer -2 to all Shaman technique
checks.
m019:
Sorcery Cultivation
Philosophy
"Reality is but rules written in qi.
Learn the language, and you can
rewrite the world.”
Sorcery Cultivation is the path of
the battle-mage, the arcane scholar
who transforms qi into raw elemental
fury and reality-bending magic. Where
other paths emphasize physical
prowess or spiritual enlightenment,
Sorcery focuses purely on
understanding and manipulating the
fundamental forces of existence
through complex techniques and
formations.
This path emerged from scholarly
cultivators who studied the underlying
principles of qi manipulation. They
discovered that by understanding the
mathematical and philosophical
principles governing reality, they could
achieve effects that seemed to violate
natural law—teleportation,
transmutation, creating matter from
nothing, bending time and space.

Sorcery cultivators are intellectuals
first and fighters second. They spend
years studying ancient texts,
experimenting with qi patterns, and
developing new techniques. Their
power comes from knowledge rather
than physical training or spiritual
refinement. A Sorcery cultivator's
greatest weapon is their mind, their
greatest defense is their preparation.
The path emphasizes three core
disciplines: Elemental Mastery,
Formation Theory, and Spell Crafting.
Sorcery cultivators excel at ranged
combat, area control, and utility
applications. They can reshape
battlefields, counter enemy techniques
through qi disruption, and solve
problems through creative application
of their vast technique repertoire.
However, they are typically fragile in
direct combat and require preparation
time to perform their most powerful
feats.

Features
Arcana, History, Investigation,
Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion
Starting Age Requirement:
14+
Primary Stats:
Perception (primary), Intelligence
(secondary), Charisma (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 6 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d6 (or
4) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: None (interferes with qi
flow), or special enchanted robes
Weapons: Staves, orbs, talismans,
simple weapons
Tools: Calligrapher's supplies,
alchemist's supplies
Saving Throws:
Perception, Intelligence
Skills:
Choose four from:
Abilities
Spellbook (LV.1)
You maintain a spellbook (or scroll
collection) containing your known
techniques. You begin knowing 6
Sorcery techniques of your choice
(GM provides list or you can design
basic ones). You can learn new
techniques by studying manuals,
observing others, or creating your own
through research.
Learning a new technique requires:
1 week of study per technique tier
DC 10 + (technique tier × 2)
Perception check
Access to reference material or a
teacher
Elemental Attunement (LV.1)
Choose two elements from: Fire,
Water, Earth, Metal, Wood, Wind,
Lightning, Ice. You have advantage on
checks related to these elements and
deal +2 damage with techniques of
these types. You can change your
attunement during a long rest.

Arcane Missiles (LV.1)
As your basic ranged attack, you
can create bolts of pure qi. Range: 60
feet. Make a ranged attack
(+Perception to hit). On hit: 1d6 +
Perception modifier force damage.
Costs 1 qi. Damage increases by level.
Counterspell (LV.3)
When you see a creature within 60
feet casting a technique, you can use
your reaction to attempt to counter it.
Spend qi equal to the technique's cost
and make an opposed Perception
check against the caster. If you win,
the technique fails and the caster's qi
is wasted.
Technique Modification (LV.3)
When you cast a technique, you
can modify it on the fly by spending
additional qi:
Empowered (+3 qi): Increase
damage by 2 dice
Extended (+2 qi): Double duration
Enlarged (+3 qi): Double area of
effect
Quickened (+4 qi): Cast as a
bonus action instead of an action
Subtle (+2 qi): Harder to
detect/counter
Formation Master (LV.5)
You can create qi formations—
semi-permanent structures of
organized qi that persist and perform
functions. Spending 10 minutes and 10
qi, you can create:
Alarm Formation: Alerts you when
creatures enter 30-foot radius
Barrier Formation: Creates wall of
force (100 HP, AC 15)
Gathering Formation: Accelerates
qi cultivation (+2 to cultivation
checks within)
Trap Formation: Deals 4d6
damage of chosen type when
triggered
Arcane Recovery (LV.9)
During a short rest, you can
recover qi through meditation and
breathing techniques. Regain qi equal
to your realm level (e.g., at 9th realm,
regain 9 qi). Can be used once per
long rest.
Spell Weaving (LV.12)
You can cast multiple techniques
simultaneously. Once per short rest,
you can cast up to three techniques as
a single action (pay qi cost for each).
Make a DC 15 Perception check:
Formations last 24 hours or until
destroyed. You can maintain
formations equal to your Perception
modifier.
Elemental Transcendence (LV.7)
You achieve mastery over your
attuned elements. When you deal
damage with a technique of your
attuned element type:
Target has disadvantage on saves
You ignore resistance to that
element
You treat immunity as resistance
Success: All techniques work as
normal
Failure: All techniques go off but
you take 2d10 force damage from
qi backlash
Critical Failure (1-5): Techniques
fail and you take 4d10 force
damage
Archmage Apotheosis (LV.15)
You have achieved the pinnacle of
Sorcery cultivation. You gain:
Technique Mastery: All technique
costs reduced by 3 qi (minimum
1)
Omnielmental: You are attuned to
ALL elements
Reality Editing: Once per long rest,
you can cast any technique
you've ever seen, regardless of
whether you know it (costs 20 qi)
Qi Pool: Your maximum qi
increases by 50
Spell Immunity: You have
advantage on saves against all
techniques and take half damage
from failed saves
Cultivation Method
Roleplay Considerations
Cultivation Method: Arcane Theory
Qi Gathering:
Sorcery cultivators cultivate
through study, experimentation, and
understanding theoretical principles.
They gain qi through meditation while
studying texts, analyzing formations,
or observing natural phenomena. Gain
+2 to cultivation checks when
cultivating in libraries, academies, or
while researching new techniques.

Academic Reputation:
Sorcery cultivators are respected
for their knowledge but sometimes
viewed as weak or overly bookish. +2
to Persuasion checks with scholars, -1
with martial cultivators.

Breakthrough Difficulty:
Hard. Your tribulations test your
understanding—you must solve qi
puzzles and prove mastery of
principles. Tribulations deal +2
damage and require passing an
Intelligence check (DC 12 + realm
level) in addition to normal saves.
Failure means breakthrough fails and
you must wait 1 month before retrying.
Technique Compatibility:
Can learn virtually any technique
given time and study. No penalties for
learning techniques from other paths,
but requires access to written manuals
or detailed observation.

Preparation Dependent:
Your effectiveness depends
heavily on preparation, study time, and
access to resources. Without your
spellbook, you suffer -3 to all
technique checks.
Resource Intensive:
Maintaining formations, conducting
research, and learning techniques
requires significant expenditure on
materials.
Fragile:
Your low HP and lack of armor
make you vulnerable in direct combat.
Rely on positioning and defensive
techniques.
m020:
Tunist Cultivation
Philosophy
"A single note can shatter
mountains. A melody can mend hearts.
A symphony can reshape reality itself.
Sound is not merely vibration—it is the
language through which the cosmos
speaks.”
Tunist Cultivation, known as Yin
Dao, is the path of those who
understand that all existence vibrates.
From the beating of a heart to the
rotation of celestial bodies, everything
produces sound—and sound, properly
harnessed, becomes power.
Tunists are cultivators who have
mastered the relationship between
sound, qi, and consciousness. They
don't simply create music; they
manipulate the fundamental
frequencies of reality. Through
instruments, voice, or even the
resonance of their own qi, Tunists can
influence emotions, alter physical
matter, heal injuries, or unleash
devastating sonic attacks.

The path originated in ancient times
when a monk named Qin Sheng
discovered that certain musical notes
corresponded to specific qi meridians.
By playing these notes in precise
sequences, he could manipulate qi flow
in his own body and others. His
disciples expanded this discovery,
creating the Seven Sacred Scales—
fundamental frequency patterns that
unlock different aspects of cultivation.
Unlike many cultivation paths that
emphasize individual power, Tunist
Cultivation recognizes that sound is
inherently communal. Music affects
both performer and listener. A Tunist's
power grows not just through personal
refinement but through understanding
harmony, resonance, and the
connections between all beings.
Tunists excel at crowd control,
emotional manipulation, healing,
environmental effects, and creating
zones of enhanced or diminished
power. They can inspire allies to
superhuman feats, drive enemies mad
with discordant melodies, or create
fields where specific types of qi
cannot function.

The greatest Tunists are said to
hear the Music of the Spheres—the
fundamental vibration of the universe
itself. By adding their own notes to this
cosmic symphony, they can perform
miracles that seem to defy natural law.
The path's primary challenge is that
sound requires space and time. A
Tunist silenced cannot fight. A Tunist
without room to perform is vulnerable.
Additionally, Tunists must guard
against Dissonance Madness—a
condition where exposure to too many
conflicting frequencies fractures the
mind.

Features
Acrobatics, Arcana, Deception,
Insight, Perception, Performance,
Persuasion, Sleight of Hand
Starting Age Requirement:
10+ (prodigies often begin young)
Primary Stats:
Charisma (primary), Perception
(secondary), Intelligence (tertiary)
Hit Points
HP at 1st Realm: 6 + Constitution
modifier
HP per Realm After 1st: 1d6 (or
4) + Constitution modifier
Armor & Weapons
Armor: Light armor (heavy armor
interferes with performance)
Weapons: Instruments (can be
used as weapons), simple
weapons, hidden blades
Tools: Musical instruments, tuning
forks, sound crystals
Saving Throws:
Charisma, Perception
Skills:
Choose four from:
Abilities
Resonant Strike (LV.1)
Your attacks carry sonic force.
When you make a weapon attack or
unarmed strike, you can spend 2 qi to
add 1d6 thunder damage. Additionally,
the target must make a Constitution
save (DC = 8 + Charisma modifier +
proficiency) or be deafened until the
end of their next turn. At higher
realms, the damage increases: 2d6 (5),
3d6 (9), 4d6 (13).
Harmonic Cultivation (LV.1)
You can cultivate through musical
practice. When you spend at least 1
hour playing music or practicing vocal
techniques, you can make a cultivation
check using Charisma instead of the
normal stat. Additionally, you gain +2
to cultivation checks when cultivating
in places with exceptional acoustics
(concert halls, echo chambers,
mountain valleys).

Song of Power (LV.1)
You learn to weave qi into your
performances, creating supernatural
effects. As an action, you can begin a
Song of Power (costs 4 qi). The song
requires concentration (as the spell)
and lasts up to 1 minute. Choose one
effect:
Valor's Anthem: All allies within
30 feet gain +1 to attack rolls and
saving throws
Dirge of Despair: All enemies
within 30 feet have disadvantage
on their next attack roll
Healing Hymn: You or one ally
within 30 feet recovers 1d6 HP at
the start of each of your turns
Speed Sonata: All allies within 30
feet gain +10 feet movement
speed
You can maintain only one Song of
Power at a time. You learn one
additional song effect at the 3rd, 5th,
7th, 9th, 12th, and 15th levels.

Perfect Pitch (LV.1)
You have absolute pitch and can
identify any sound you hear. You gain
advantage on Perception checks
involving sound. Additionally, you can
mimic any sound or voice you've
heard with a successful DC 12
Performance check.
Sonic Pulse (LV.3)
Once per short rest, you can
release a pulse of concentrated sound.
As an action, spend 5 qi. All creatures
within 15 feet must make a
Constitution save (DC = 8 + Charisma
modifier + proficiency) or take 3d8
thunder damage and be pushed 10 feet
away. On a successful save, they take
half damage and aren't pushed.
The damage increases to 5d8 at 7th
realm, 7d8 at 11th realm, and 9d8 at
15th realm. The radius increases by 5
feet every 4 realms.
Resonate (LV.3)
You can match the vibrational
frequency of objects and beings. As an
action, spend 3 qi and make a
Performance check:
DC 12: You can cause nonmagical objects to vibrate
violently (shattering glass,
loosening bonds, opening locks)
DC 15: You can sense structural
weaknesses in buildings or
formations
DC 18: You can resonate with a
creature's qi, learning basic
information about them
(cultivation level, general
emotional state, presence of
curses/diseases)
DC 20+: You can shatter nonmagical objects of significant size
(doors, walls, weapons)
Sound Shape (LV.5)
You can solidify sound into
physical constructs. As an action,
spend 6 qi to create a construct of
solidified sound that lasts for 1 minute.
You can create:
Sound Barrier: A wall of sonic
energy (20 feet long, 10 feet high,
AC 15, 50 HP) that blocks
movement and sound
Sound Servant: A humanoid figure
that can perform simple tasks (HP
30, +6 to hit, 1d10 force damage)
Sound Platform: A disc you can
ride (diameter 10 feet, flies at 40
feet per round, carries up to 500
lbs)
You can have only one Sound
Shape active at a time. Additional uses
require spending the qi cost again.

Your Songs of Power become
significantly more potent. You can now
maintain concentration on a Song of
Power even while taking other actions
(including attacking or using other
techniques). Additionally, when you
begin a Song of Power, you can affect
allies within 60 feet instead of 30 feet.
You learn advanced song effects:
Dissonant Countermeasure (LV.5)
You can disrupt enemy techniques
with dissonant frequencies. As a
reaction when a creature within 60
feet casts a technique or uses an
ability, spend 5 qi and make a
Performance check contested by their
technique attack roll or save DC. If
you win, their technique fails and the
qi is wasted.
You can use this ability a number
of times per long rest equal to your
Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
Master's Performance (LV.7)
Thunder Canon: One enemy within
60 feet takes 4d10 thunder
damage (Constitution save for
half)
Silence Shroud: Create a 20-foot
radius zone where no sound can
occur (friend or foe)
Mass Inspiration: All allies within
60 feet gain temporary HP equal
to your Charisma modifier × 2
Fear Frequency: All enemies
within 60 feet must make a
Charisma save or become
frightened for 1 minute
Sympathetic Vibration (LV.7)
You understand how to make one
object resonate with another. When
you successfully hit a creature with a
Resonant Strike, you can mark them
for 1 minute (costs no additional qi).
While marked, any thunder or force
damage they take from any source
deals an additional 1d8 damage as
your initial vibration amplifies
subsequent impacts. You can maintain
this mark on a number of creatures
equal to your Charisma modifier.
Sonic Sanctuary (LV.9)
You can create a zone of
controlled acoustics. As an action,
spend 10 qi to create a 30-foot radius
sphere centered on you that lasts for
10 minutes. Within this sphere:
You choose what sounds occur
(you can silence enemies, prevent
sound-based techniques, allow
ally communication while enemies
hear nothing)
All thunder damage dealt by you
or allies increases by +1d6
All Charisma-based checks by
you or allies gain +2
You can sense the exact location
of all creatures within the sphere
The sphere moves with you. You
can dismiss it as a bonus action.
Voice of Command (LV.9)
As an action, spend 8 qi and speak
a one-word command to a creature
within 60 feet. They must make a
Charisma save (DC = 10 + your
Charisma modifier + proficiency) or
obey the command on their next turn if
physically possible. Commands can be:
Flee, Halt, Drop, Approach, Grovel,
Sleep, Confess, etc.
This ability doesn't work on
creatures that can't hear you or are
immune to charm effects. You can use
this ability a number of times per long
rest equal to your Charisma modifier.

Soundless Form (LV.12)
As an action, spend 8 qi to enter
Soundless Form for up to 1 hour.
While in this state:
You produce absolutely no sound
(footsteps, breathing, heartbeat,
etc.)
You gain advantage on all Stealth
checks
You have resistance to thunder
damage
As a bonus action, you can
become completely invisible for 1
round (but reappear if you attack)
You can end this state as a bonus
action.
Worldsong (LV.15)
You have learned to hear and
manipulate the fundamental frequency
of reality itself. You gain the following
permanent benefits:
You can hear sounds from up to 1
mile away if you concentrate
You automatically detect illusions,
invisible creatures, and hidden
passages within 100 feet (sound
reveals all)
You can communicate
telepathically with any creature
within 1 mile by "playing"
thoughts into their mind
Once per long rest, you can
perform the Grand Crescendo—a
reality-warping performance
Grand Crescendo (Ultimate
Technique)
As a 10-minute performance, spend
25 qi. You can achieve one of the
following effects:
Heal all allies within 1 mile for
10d10 HP and remove all curses,
diseases, and poisons
Deal 15d10 thunder damage to all
enemies within 500 feet
(Constitution save for half)
Reshape the environment within
500 feet (create walls, bridges, or
destroy structures)
Break any curse, seal, or
formation within 1 mile by finding
its resonant frequency
Summon a Celestial Spirit of music
to fight on your behalf for 10
minutes (CR 15 equivalent)
Cultivation Method
Cultivation Method: Harmonic
Resonance
Qi Gathering:
Tunists cultivate by achieving
harmony between their internal qi and
external vibrations. They gain qi
through musical practice, meditation on
natural sounds (waterfalls, wind,
thunder), and performing for
audiences. The more people who hear
and appreciate a Tunist's music, the
more qi they can draw from the
collective resonance.
Gain +3 to cultivation checks when
cultivating in acoustically rich
environments or immediately after a
successful performance before an
audience of 10+ people.
Breakthrough Difficulty:
Medium-High. Your tribulations
manifest as Dissonance Challenges—
you must find harmony within chaos.
Tribulations produce overwhelming
cacophonies that threaten to shatter
your mind and meridians.

During breakthroughs, you take
standard tribulation damage but can
reduce it by 1d10 for each successful
Performance check (DC = 10 + new
realm level, maximum 3 checks per
tribulation). However, failure on a
check causes an additional 1d6
psychic damage as dissonance tears at
your consciousness.
Technique Compatibility:
Easily learns sound, music, wind,
and emotion-based techniques (+2
to learning checks)
Synergizes well with illusion and
mental techniques (+1 to learning
checks)
Struggles with earth, silence, and
anti-magic techniques (-3 to
learning checks)
Cannot learn techniques that
require absolute silence or
stillness to perform
Roleplay Considerations
Musical Instruments:
Your choice of instrument defines
your style. Stringed instruments
(guqin, pipa) excel at precision and
subtle manipulation. Wind instruments
(flute, xiao) favor mobility and area
effects. Percussion (drums) delivers
raw power but less control. Voice is
the most versatile but requires you to
be able to speak.

Dissonance Madness:
If you're exposed to too many
conflicting high-frequency techniques
in rapid succession, you risk
Dissonance Madness. After taking 50+
thunder damage in a single encounter,
make a Charisma save (DC 15). On a
failure, you suffer confusion (as the
spell) for 1d4 rounds. Repeated
failures can cause permanent hearing
damage or mental instability.

Performance Requirements:
Many of your abilities require that
enemies can hear you. Deafened
creatures, soundproof barriers, and
zones of silence severely limit your
power. Fighting underwater or in a
vacuum is nearly impossible for lowerrealm Tunists.

Ethical Questions:
Your abilities to manipulate
emotions and command obedience
raise moral questions. A Tunist who
uses Voice of Command to force
confessions or changes hearts with
music must grapple with the nature of
free will.

Social Dynamics:
Tunists are often beloved by
common folk (entertainers, joybringers) but can be dismissed by
martial cultivators as "mere
musicians." This creates interesting
social tension. However, smart
cultivators respect Tunists—everyone
knows the story of the Tunist who
played a single note that collapsed an
entire siege tower.

Instrument Maintenance:
Your cultivation tool is your
instrument. A damaged or poorly
maintained instrument reduces your
effectiveness (GM may impose
disadvantage on Performance checks).
Ancient, well-crafted, or spiritually
attuned instruments can enhance your
power (+1 to +3 to Performance
checks or technique DCs).
